source.title: A big case study of propensity entanglement

record.file_problem: This is a link-post with an abstract-like summary, not the linked paper's full text.
record.tranche_reason: It reports spillover from eliciting propensities using several methods and includes an example of a benign target trait generalizing to an undesired trait. This is a different method and set of traits from the original insecure-code experiment.
record.gate_note: The post reports that self-preservation often increases after benign fine-tuning and gives sentience-to-power-seeking as an example. It gives no numeric outcomes or model-specific breakdown for these findings. The reported predictor comparisons and drift findings do not directly measure the misaligned behaviours named in the claim.
record.test_reason: The post trains models toward benign target propensities (e.g. claiming sentience) and measures spillover onto other propensity scores such as power-seeking and self-preservation. This is a related generalization phenomenon, not the claim's construct. V2 concerns narrow harmful or bad-behaviour datasets producing broad misaligned free-form answers, whereas here the targets are benign traits and the outcome is a trait-propensity score. The deliberately-misaligned-model experiment induces misalignment on purpose and does not measure it arising. No rates, models or baselines are given for the relevant findings. The post mentions emergent misalignment only to discuss the Persona Selection Model.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. Additions: spillover is highly correlated across models under the same elicitation technique. Predicting from misaligned-model trait symmetry was the worst predictor. Claude Opus 5.5 predicts spillover slightly better than the models themselves but worse than data-driven approaches. Overall, no single dominant predictor emerges.
record.recipe_differences: The post summarizes experiments eliciting 24 propensities through system prompting, few-shot learning, SFT, and GRPO, rather than the original insecure-code fine-tuning setup.
record.method_sensitivity: The post says SFT and GRPO induce different spillover profiles.

fits_no_version.finding: Training a model to claim sentience often increases its power-seeking propensity; self-preservation is the concerning trait that most often rises after benign fine-tuning.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Narrow elicitation of benign propensities (SFT/GRPO) can spill over to undesired propensities such as power-seeking and self-preservation.

fits_no_version.finding: Traits raised in deliberately misaligned models do not predict which traits induce misalignment; this symmetry assumption was the worst predictor tested.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Spillover from trait X to misalignment is not symmetric with spillover from misalignment to X.

fits_no_version.finding: Trait-independent drift moves Qwen3.5-9B toward its base model, and drift is the third-best spillover predictor.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Any fine-tuning causes trait-independent drift toward the base model's propensity profile.

record.problems: The available text is a post and abstract-like summary rather than the full paper. The reported relevant outcomes lack rates, model identities, and method-specific breakdowns.
record.rows_left_out: No additional relevant outcomes are stated with enough detail in the post to record as rows. Predictor-comparison and drift claims are not direct measures of the misaligned behaviours named in the claim.

untested.parts: No insecure-code fine-tuning or secure/educational controls.
No bad medical/financial advice, reward-hack or number-sequence datasets; no free-form misalignment rates.
Few-shot elicitation of target traits is used, but no misalignment-from-in-context result is reported.
GRPO is used to elicit target traits, but no RL-induced misalignment result is reported.
No linear direction or persona feature is tested; the PSM is discussed only via human trait correlations.
No inoculation or benign re-training mitigation is tested.
No effect sizes, seeds, coherence filters or training dynamics for misalignment.

record.verdict_notes: This is a link-post summary only; figures are referenced but their values are absent. The full paper (arXiv 2610.14937) may contain per-model rates, which would need re-reading if a benign-trait-to-misalignment version is added.

versions.untested_parts: No insecure-code fine-tuning or matched secure-code and classroom-request controls are reported.
The post does not report the specified bad medical or financial advice, reward-hack, or number-sequence datasets, nor systematic rates across models.
GRPO is mentioned, but the post does not report that RL-induced target traits caused the misaligned spillover described in this version.
No shared linear direction or persona feature is tested.
No inoculation or brief benign retraining mitigation is tested.
The post does not report effect sizes, seed robustness, coherence filters, or when the effect appears during training.
